 Metals Gold edges lower ahead of Fed rate decision, Warsh comments
 Published Wed, Oct 28 2026 12:33 AM EDT Updated 50 Min Ago WATCH LIVE In this article
 @GC26Z 
 Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT Gold prices ticked lower on Wednesday after the previous session's climb of about 1%, as higher oil prices stoked inflation fears while investors awaited the Federal Reserve's policy decision later in the day for clues to the rate outlook. Edgar Su | Reuters 
Gold was subdued on Wednesday as higher oil prices weighed on sentiment, while market participants awaited ​the U.S. Federal Reserve's policy ​decision and comments from ​Chairman Kevin Warsh for clues on the path of interest rates.
 Spot gold edged 0.3% lower to $4,044.54 an ounce, while U.S. gold futures for December delivery fell 0.4% ⁠to $4,057.30 ‌per ounce.
 The U.S. central bank will announce its ⁠rate decision at 2 p.m. EDT, followed by a press conference by the Fed chief.
 "We see a very low likelihood that the U.S. central bank is going to lift rates today, but December is ‌on, March is on as well. So for now, [prices] stay anchored to the lower bound of the range," Bart Melek, global head of commodity ​strategy at TD Securities, said.
 The Fed is widely expected to leave its benchmark interest rate unchanged in the 3.75%-4.00% range, with traders pricing in an 84% probability of a hike in December, according to the CME's FedWatch tool.
 Attention is also ⁠turning to U.S. Personal Consumption Expenditures data due on Thursday, which could offer further insight into the ‌trajectory of monetary policy.
 Meanwhile, oil prices rose over 1%, ‌stoking inflation concerns, after an attack on a refinery in Saudi Arabia renewed concerns about supply risks linked to war in the Middle East.
 "Higher inflation ultimately means that the Fed will be forced ⁠to take decisive action in December and in March. And beyond that, much will ⁠depend on how quickly the conflict in the Middle East comes ⁠to some sort of resolution," Melek added.
 Higher rates increase the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding gold.
 Analysts lowered their 2026 precious metals price forecasts in ​Reuters polls, citing weaker demand, elevated ‌Treasury yields and a strong U.S. dollar, though all the metals are still expected to rebound in 2027.
 Elsewhere, China's net gold imports via Hong Kong in September rose more than 28% from August to a five-month high, due to restocking ahead of the Golden Week holiday, with additional support from ​investor demand.
 Among other metals, spot silver slid ‌1.2% to $53.71 per ounce, platinum gained 0.2% to $1,542.80, and palladium fell 0.7% to $1,019.03.
